WMU 504 Aerial Ungulate  Survey Report (2015) 
Background 
The last survey conducted for WMU 504 was  completed in February 2007,  using the random 
stratified block methodology  (prioritizing moose)  and produced a  moose population estimate of 
1,460 moose (±404, 90% confidence interval) and a white-tailed deer population estimate of 3,580 
(no confidence intervals were determined).  The population goal for moose in WMU 504 is 800  and 
for white-tailed deer is 3,500. The ‘Archery Only’ season for most big game is fr om September 1 to 
October 31 and the ‘General’ season is from November 1 to 30. Antlered  and antlerless moose are 
managed on a limited entry hunt in both the ‘Archery Only’ and ‘General’ seasons in WMU 504. The 
2015 hunting season  is the first year that mo ose hunting during the ‘Archery Only’  season will 
require a special license . Prior to 201 5 all cohorts of moose were available for unlimited ‘Archery 
Only’ season harvest with the general moose license. Mule deer (antlered and antlerless) are also 
managed through a limited entry ‘General’ season hunt. Hunting antlered mule deer in the ‘Archery 
Only’ season requires a special license  while antlerless mule deer may be hunted under a general 
license in the ‘Archery Only’  season.  White -tailed deer (antlered  and antlerless) are managed 
under ‘Archery Only’ and ‘General’ seasons, both only requiring a general license ; no supplemental 
antlerless white-tailed deer tags can be used in WMU  504 as these licenses were eliminated in 
2011. Elk are available for harvest in WMU 504 as well; 3+ point bulls may be harvested during the 
‘Archery Only’ season and during the ‘General’ season under the authority of a general license, and 
antlerless elk may be harvested during the ‘Archery Only’  season under a general license  but 
require a special license for the ‘General’ season. 
Survey Method 
The objective of this survey was to establish population estimates for mo ose, white-tailed and to 
obtain useful information on mule deer  and elk to guide management of these species .  Collection 
of age data and sex data was conducted where possible. Given this survey took place in early 
January it is suspected that antler cast  was minimal (estimated at 15% based on local trail camera 
monitoring and public feedback). As a result, antlerless adult deer with fawns was classified as does 
but many antlerless adults were classified without sex information .  T ransects, 10 km i n length (at 
times shorter when the lines ran into WMU boundaries) and oriented east -west, were established 
spatially throughout the WMU at 1.2 km intervals within  a GIS environment.  Based on previous 
survey ungulate densities, transects were randomly selected until a minimum of 500 kilometres of 
survey distance was achieved.  The survey was then flown using distance sampling me thodology as 
described in the Distance Sampling Chapter of the Aerial Ungulate Survey Protocol Manual (ESRD, 
2014).   
Results 
The survey was completed from January 6 to 11 , 2015. Total ungulates observed were 321 moose, 
273 white-tailed deer, 24 mule deer and 14 elk. Of the 264 moose that were successfully classified, 
115 were cows, 78 were calves, 45 were antlered bulls and 26 were non-antlered bulls.  Sixty-three 
white-tailed deer were unable to be classified; 20 bucks were classified along with 115 does and 75  
fawns. Of the 21  mule deer that were successfully classified, 13 were does, 6 were fawns, and 2 
were bucks.  Of the 8 elk that were successfully classified 1 was a bull, 5 were cows and 2 were
